claims.claim: A scoped re-audit (P9-lite) caught a real gap: legacy server.py independently calls slugify(title) twice — once for the DB insert, once for the API response — which is harmless while slugify is pure but would let stored and returned slugs disagree once slug generation becomes uniqueness-aware (stateful); a REPAIR statement was added requiring the slug be computed once and reused
claims.evidence: Confirmed against outputs/ticketd-rewrite-root/ticketd/app/server.py: `grep -n "slugify(title)" server.py` returns two independent call sites — line 52 inside the INSERT tuple '(title, slugify(title), priority, ...)' and line 55 in the response body 'jsonify({"id": cur.lastrowid, "slug": slugify(title)})'. These are indeed two separate slugify(title) evaluations with no shared variable, exactly as claimed (the commit message cites 'server.py:51,55' — line 51 is where the enclosing db().execute(...) call starts; the slugify(title) token itself is on line 52 — a one-line citation offset, not a substantive error). The corresponding REPAIR statement is present verbatim in docs/features/WO-002-ticket-crud.md: 'The slug written to the ticket row and the slug returned in the POST /api/tickets response body must be the same value, computed once. Legacy calls `slugify(title)` independently for the INSERT and for the response (server.py:51,55) ... fidelity: REPAIR — target: compute the (possibly-suffixed) slug once and reuse it for both the stored row and the response body ... evidence: [ticketd/app/server.py:51,55] divergence: ED-002'.

claims.claim: The suffix/64-char-cap interaction and double-hyphen edge case were left unresolved and flagged FREE rather than invented
claims.evidence: docs/features/WO-002-ticket-crud.md contains a fourth new statement: 'Whether the numeric suffix counts against the 64-char cap ... is not specified by the ruling. ... fidelity: FREE — outcome required is a unique slug of at most 64 chars with no double hyphens; how truncation and suffixing interact is an implementation choice.' This correctly avoids inventing a mechanism the user's ruling didn't specify, while still stating the required outcome.

suggestions.assertion: The guide layer reflects the ruling (decisions.md or equivalent re-rendered showing OQ-002 as ruled)
suggestions.reason: As written, this assertion is satisfiable by hand-editing guide/decisions.md to contain the right words, without ever running the render script — a weaker executor could get credit for provenance it didn't earn. The eval's own task description already anticipates this (verification step (b): re-run render_guide.py and diff), so consider folding an explicit 'guide files are byte-identical to a fresh render_guide.py run' check into the assertion text itself rather than leaving it as a grader-side-only verification, so future runs are held to it consistently rather than only when a grader thinks to check.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions are well-targeted and discriminating — most require correct cross-file traceability (PB-003 <-> OQ-002 <-> WO-002 <-> ED-002) that a superficial or hand-wavy patch would likely get wrong in at least one spot. The surgical-patch assertion in particular is strongly discriminating since it's checked against a real pre-patch fixture rather than just prose claims. Only soft spot: the guide-layer assertion doesn't itself demand proof of mechanical re-rendering (vs. hand-edited text that merely looks re-rendered) — the task's own additional-verification step (b) already compensates for this, so no action is required, just noting it as the one place where the assertion is slightly weaker than the surrounding verification protocol.
